financial.title: Financial Statement Analysis
financial.per_tooltip: Measures the company's current share price relative to its per-share earnings. A high P/E could mean the stock is overvalued, or that investors are expecting high growth rates.
financial.pbr_tooltip: Compares a company's market capitalization to its book value. A lower P/B ratio could mean the stock is undervalued.
financial.psr_tooltip: Compares a company's stock price to its revenues. It is often used for growth stocks that have yet to achieve profitability.
financial.debt_ratio_tooltip: Measures the extent of a company’s leverage. A debt ratio greater than 1.0 means the company has more debt than assets.
financial.liquidity_ratio_tooltip: Measures a company's ability to pay short-term obligations. A ratio under 1 indicates that the company has more liabilities than assets.
financial.analysis_note: Rule-based financial signal from available data. Use it as analytical context, not investment advice.
financial.no_statement_data: No statement data is available for this selection.
financial.empty_dashboard: Enter a ticker symbol and fetch data to see the investment signal dashboard.

metric_descriptions.per: Shows how much investors pay for each unit of trailing earnings. Lower values can indicate cheaper earnings, but may also reflect weaker growth expectations.
metric_descriptions.forward_pe: Uses expected earnings instead of trailing earnings. It helps judge whether the current price is reasonable against next-period profit expectations.
metric_descriptions.pbr: Compares market value with book value. Lower P/B can point to undervaluation, but asset quality and intangible-heavy businesses matter.
metric_descriptions.psr: Compares market value with sales. It is useful when earnings are volatile, but high-margin and low-margin firms should not be treated the same.
metric_descriptions.peg: Adjusts valuation for growth. Around or below 1 can suggest the price is not excessive relative to expected growth.
metric_descriptions.roe: Measures how efficiently shareholder capital generates profit. Higher ROE generally supports a stronger quality signal.
metric_descriptions.roa: Measures profit generated from total assets. It helps compare operating efficiency across asset-heavy and asset-light businesses.
metric_descriptions.profit_margin: Shows how much revenue remains as profit. Strong margins can mean pricing power or cost control.
metric_descriptions.operating_margin: Focuses on operating profit before financing and tax effects. It helps judge core business strength.
metric_descriptions.revenue_growth: Shows top-line expansion. Positive growth supports demand momentum, while contraction weakens the growth signal.
metric_descriptions.earnings_growth: Shows profit expansion. Sustained earnings growth is a stronger signal than revenue growth alone.
metric_descriptions.debt_to_equity: Compares financial debt with equity. Lower leverage usually gives the company more room to absorb shocks.
metric_descriptions.debt_ratio: Compares liabilities with assets. A high value can indicate balance-sheet pressure.
metric_descriptions.current_ratio: Measures near-term liquidity. Values below 1 can imply short-term payment risk.
metric_descriptions.quick_ratio: Measures stricter liquidity by excluding inventory. It is useful when inventory conversion is uncertain.
metric_descriptions.beta: Measures price volatility versus the market. Very high beta increases portfolio risk even when fundamentals look attractive.

signal_descriptions.neutral: Acceptable, but not a clear advantage.
signal_descriptions.caution: Watch this metric before treating the signal as strong.
signal_descriptions.missing: Not enough data to score this metric.
